outcome: Latency period (time from PPROM to delivery)
cohort: The study included 698 women (101 twin pregnancies and 597 singleton pregnancies) admitted with PPROM between 24-34 weeks of gestation.
finding: PPROM in twin pregnancies tends to occur at a more advanced gestational age, is associated with a shorter latency period, and is less likely to be complicated by chorioamnionitis or placental abruption compared with singletons.
gest_age: Participants were admitted with PPROM between 24-34 weeks of gestation; twins presented at 29.1 ± 2.7 weeks and singletons at 28.5 ± 2.8 weeks.
